analysis.one_liner: Adani Power is India's largest private thermal power generator, selling electricity to state utilities under long-term PPAs and to the merchant/exchange market.
analysis.whats_happening: Adani Power reported Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) results on 23 October 2026 - consolidated net profit jumped ~142% YoY to Rs 7,019 crore and revenue rose 29.8% to Rs 17,014 crore. A large chunk of that profit came from a one-time Rs 2,422 crore prior-period revenue recognition tied to historical PPA tariff-charge adjustments, so the headline growth rate is not fully repeatable. Despite the beat, the stock is down about 25% from its May 2026 high amid a broader correction across power-sector stocks.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a thermal power company that builds and runs coal plants and sells the electricity, mostly under long-term contracts with state power boards. The quarter's reported profit growth of 142% sounds dramatic, but a meaningful part of it is a one-off accounting catch-up, not new ongoing business - strip that out and underlying operating profit (EBITDA) grew a more modest 18.5%. The company is also now borrowing more to fund an ambitious plan to roughly triple capacity by 2032, so the real question for shareholders is whether that growth pays off faster than the debt builds up.
analysis.quarters: Sales volume rose 11.5% YoY to 26.4 billion units and plant load factor improved sharply from 62.8% to 70.1%, showing genuine volume-led demand strength. However, revenue growth of 29.8% and profit growth of 142% both include a Rs 2,422 crore one-time prior-period revenue item linked to PPA tariff-charge adjustments - management itself separated this out, and EBITDA excluding one-offs grew a more modest 18.5% to Rs 6,321 crore. Management reiterated a plan to grow generation capacity from 18 GW to 42 GW by 2032, with 6,120 MW under construction for FY27-FY29 commissioning and long-term PPAs already signed for about 62% of its 24 GW thermal pipeline.
analysis.performance_read: Returns have been exceptional on paper: +163% over 3 years and +731% over 5 years versus the Nifty's +19% and +25% respectively. A 5:1 stock split in September 2025 is already reflected in these rebased figures, so this is genuine market re-rating, not a split artifact. That said, the stock is down 25.1% from its 27 May 2026 peak of Rs 248.91, and over the last 3 months it has fallen roughly in line with peer NTPC (-12.8% vs -13.6%) as the broader power sector corrected - this looks like sector-wide profit-taking after a steep run-up rather than a company-specific breakdown.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades at a P/E of roughly 26x, a premium to the sector peer median (cited around 21x). That premium is partly justified by genuinely high return ratios (ROE 21.9%, ROCE 24%), but it is also pricing in execution of the 18 GW-to-42 GW capacity ambition, which carries multi-year funding and commissioning risk. Price-to-book figures found across sources ranged wildly from under 1x to nearly 7x, likely reflecting inconsistent updates to book value per share after the September 2025 stock split - this figure is not verified and should be checked directly on Screener rather than relied on from any single source here.
analysis.growth_read: Growth this quarter was both volume-led (units sold up 11.5%, PLF up nearly 7.3 percentage points) and price/tariff-led, which is a healthier combination than margin expansion alone. But investors should not extrapolate the 29.8% revenue or 142% profit growth rates forward - a meaningful slice of both is the one-time PPA-related revenue recognition that management flagged as non-recurring.
analysis.health_read: Operating profitability is strong (EBITDA growth of 18.5% ex-one-offs, ROCE of 24%), suggesting profits are largely converting into operating cash. The real pressure point is financial, not operational: total debt rose from Rs 53,555 crore to Rs 61,860 crore in just six months (+15%) as the company funds its expansion pipeline. Debt-to-equity at 0.82 is much improved from 3.33 in FY23, but it is set to climb again as the 6,120 MW under-construction capacity gets built out - this is a financing/execution risk tied to the growth plan, not a sign of a weak core business.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding is stable at 74.96% with a low pledge of 1.81% - no governance red flag on the pledging front. FII holding slipped slightly from 11.76% to 11.03% over the quarter while mutual fund holding rose from 3.92% to 4.31%. No marquee independent investor was found on the shareholding register in available sources - not verified, worth checking directly. Separately, the personal US bribery/fraud indictment against group chairman Gautam Adani was dismissed by a US federal judge in August 2026, removing a Group-level legal overhang, though this is an Adani Group development rather than something specific to Adani Power's own filings.
strengths: ROCE of 24% and ROE of 21.9%, well above typical thermal-power-sector returns
Sales volume up 11.5% YoY with plant load factor improving from 62.8% to 70.1%
Promoter pledge minimal at 1.81% with holding steady at ~75%
Long-term PPAs already secured for about 62% of its 24 GW upcoming thermal pipeline, giving revenue visibility
watchpoints: Total debt rose 15% in just six months (Rs 53,555 crore to Rs 61,860 crore) to fund capacity expansion
Headline 142% profit growth included a Rs 2,422 crore one-time prior-period revenue item; underlying EBITDA growth was a more modest 18.5%
Stock trades at a P/E premium to sector peers (~26x vs ~21x median) despite falling 25% from its May 2026 peak
Execution risk on the 18 GW-to-42 GW by 2032 target, which depends on sustained capex, financing and timely PPA signing
analysis.one_thing: Whether EBITDA/profit growth holds near the ex-one-off rate of ~18.5% once the Rs 2,422 crore one-time PPA-adjustment item rolls off in coming quarters, and whether debt growth stays proportionate as the 6,120 MW under-construction capacity is commissioned through FY27-FY29.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue/profit figures cross-checked across BusinessToday, Business Standard and other news coverage of the 23 October 2026 results. ROE, ROCE and P/E figures sourced from gurufocus-linked commentary; promoter holding and pledge data from Trendlyne-based shareholding pattern reports. P/B ratio could not be reliably verified - sources returned inconsistent values (roughly 1x to 7x), likely due to uneven post-split book-value updates; treat as unverified and check Screener directly. Dividend data not available (TTM dividend null) - only a token payment on preference shares was found for FY26.
